back: It adds many small trees one by one. Each new tree predicts the remaining errors of the current model, scaled by a learning rate.

front: Which objective for non-negative skewed sales with zeros?
back: Tweedie (power between 1 and 2) or Poisson. They model the mean with a log link and never predict negatives.

front: How do you get prediction intervals with boosting?
back: Train one model per quantile with the quantile (pinball) objective, for example 0.1, 0.5 and 0.9.

front: Safe early stopping for time series?
back: Validate on the newest part of the training period, never on a random split or the test set.

front: Why can trees not extrapolate a trend?
back: Each leaf holds an average of training targets. Predict a change or ratio, or detrend, to stay inside the range.

front: Best way to read feature importance?
back: Use permutation importance on out-of-time data, and treat a dominant feature as a possible leak, not as proof of cause.
